title: Three-point polar alignment divides by a zero intermediate for solvable geometry
summary: Category functional; severity medium; confidence high; owner coordinator; open, nonblocking follow-up. indigo_libs/indigo_align.c:702-710 solves the two equations using v=(d3k1-d2k3)/(k4k1-k2k3) then u=(d2-vk2)/k1. When the first two hour angles are symmetric around the meridian (e.g -15°, +15°, followed by +45°), k1=cos(a2)-cos(a1)=0 although the determinant can be nonzero and the system remains solvable. The final division yields nonfinite u while returning true; near-symmetry is also poorly conditioned. This is a legitimate three-distinct-point polar alignment geometry. The actual platesolver reference3 path685 ignores the boolean and694-698 publishes the resulting state OK, passing error values into target coordinate generation692-693. Solve both outputs directly using the determinant (or choose a stable pivot), reject genuinely singular/nonfinite results, and require the caller to honor failure before publishing a target/OK. Next: coordinator assigns scoped remediation and regression verification; full evidence/remedy in findings.md (MATH-2). No fix or risk acceptance claimed.
